content: Lymphomas are the third most frequently occurring malignancy in children. While cure rates for childhood lymphoma are high, they have reached a plateau, indicating the need for the development of new treatment strategies. Antibody therapy has emerged as a successful and innovative treatment option for adult lymphoma. However, none of the therapeutic antibodies currently approved for adult cancer treatment have been approved for use in paediatric lymphoma. The objective of this review was to evaluate the efficacy of antibody therapy in children with lymphoma, specifically in terms of survival rates, treatment response, and relapse rates, as compared to conventional therapies that do not include antibody treatment. Additionally, the review aimed to assess the quality of life and the incidence of adverse effects associated with antibody therapy in children, in comparison to non-antibody-based treatments. To gather relevant data, a comprehensive search was conducted across multiple databases, including the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL, 2014, Issue 10), MEDLINE in PubMed (from 1945 to October 2014), and EMBASE (from 1980 to October 2014). Reference lists of pertinent articles were also reviewed. Furthermore, abstracts from conference proceedings of SIOP, ASCO, and ASH (spanning 2009 to 2013) were examined, along with ongoing trials listed in the World Health Organization (WHO) ICTRP portal and ClinicalTrials.gov. The inclusion criteria for this review were randomised controlled trials and controlled clinical trials that compared conventional therapy with antibody therapy in paediatric lymphoma patients. Two independent authors conducted the study selection process. No studies meeting the inclusion criteria were identified during the review process. Consequently, it is currently not possible to draw evidence-based conclusions regarding the clinical application of antibody therapy in paediatric lymphoma. However, early-phase studies (Phase I and II) have demonstrated promising effects of antibody therapy in children with lymphoma. Further research is essential to thoroughly evaluate the efficacy and safety of antibody therapy and to facilitate its implementation in the treatment of paediatric lymphoma.
